newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Turnpike says nearing pact for hotel complex.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Turnpike says nearing pact for hotel complex.

text.p: The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority has said that it was moving closer towards a pact on air rights with a developer for a $300 million retail and hotel complex near Massachusetts Avenue in Boston.

Chairman James Kerasiotes told reporters in Boston on Tuesday that New York-based Millennium Partners was exploring environmental and design issues. Its exclusive rights to the site expire next month.
Boston Mayor Thomas Menino has objected to the deal, saying the Turnpike was starting development without getting the city's views. Kerasiotes said public hearings would begin early next month.

The Turnpike official also is negotiating over a role in a 20-story apartment development that would be located near the Back Bay train station. About 20 percent of the 280 to 300 apartments would be subsidized.

The board approved a "stand still" agreement with Arthur Winn, a Boston developer, giving him exclusive rights to the parcel until May 1. Winn has given the Turnpike a $150,000 deposit and another $25,000 for any further expenses it incurs during negotiations.

Finally, the Turnpike chairman said that a plan to close westbound toll booths in Newton and Boston would not cause the road to lose any revenues because the tolls of drivers heading east into Boston would be doubled to $1. Motorists heading into Boston would pay $1 at an exchange with Route 128 and another $1 at Allston.
